children: Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials) is broadening its AI approach beyond processors with a new open rack plan for large-scale agentic AI infrastructure.

The platform, named AMD Helion, is built on Open Compute Project standards and offers variable combinations of CPUs and GPUs. This concerns because AI infrastructure is increasingly being purchased as an integrated system rather just chips.
A Helion setup with just CPUs with sixth-generation EPYC processors can expand to 32,768 CPU cores. Another arrangement pairs EPYC CPUs with Instinct MI350P GPUs for business agentic AI applications.
Also, customers can select air-cooled or liquid-cooled designs according to their performance, power and cost needs.

The potential for AMD is to make its technology easier to deploy in more sorts of artificial intelligence systems and reduce the friction customers have when combining CPUs, GPUs and current IT infrastructure.
The business also aims to donate the Helion specification to the Open Compute Project community, which may help drive broader adoption.

The program is backed by Cisco, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro and numerous more hardware partners. But the main question for investors is whether AMD can convert that ecosystem support into a better competitive position in AI infrastructure, where Nvidia currently dominates much of the accelerator market.
The next trigger is in November when Helion rack configurations are scheduled to begin becoming accessible via ecosystem partners.

title: AMD Wants a Bigger Piece of the AI Stack
